title: Cap. X Arg. X: suspending gifts on prior littleness is Pelagian unless littleness itself is God’s special gift — Orange canon 6; preparing littleness for one is electing
pass_a_gloss: Next, those who suspend these gifts of God from preceding littleness, unless they confess that this very littleness is a special gift of God, fall into Pelagianism, and run upon Canon 6 of the Council of Orange: But if they confess it, it is all one to grant that God prepared and gave this littleness, whence faith and salvation hang, unto one and not unto the other, and prepared and gave faith itself and salvation; which is nothing other than to have elected one, to have reprobated the other.
pass_b_english: Next: those who hang these gifts on prior littleness, unless they admit that littleness itself is God’s special gift, fall into Pelagianism and hit Orange canon 6. If they do admit it, that is the same as granting God prepared and gave that littleness—on which faith and salvation hang—to one and not the other, and prepared and gave faith and salvation themselves; which is nothing other than electing one and reprobating the other.
source_text: Dein, qui haec dona Dei suspendunt ex parvitate praeeunte, nisi fateantur hanc ipsam parvitatem esse speciale donum Dei, in Pelagianismum incidunt, et incurrunt in Canonem 6. Concilii Arausicani: Si autem fateantur, perinde est concedere Deum praeparasse et donasse hanc parvitatem, unde fides et salus dependet, uni et non alteri, atque praeparasse et donasse ipsam fidem et salutem; quod nihil aliud est, quam unum elegisse, alterum reprobasse.
